clue.text: State we hear spelt without consonants?

definitions.text: State we hear spelt without consonants?

parts.words: State we hear spelt without consonants?
parts.note: said aloud, this US state sounds like a string of vowel sounds, as if spelt with no consonants at all

explanation.surface: A quiz question about which American state could be written down using only vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, IOWA sounds like the letters I, O, A with only a glide between them. The W is the one consonant, and you barely hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a Midwestern US state whose pronunciation is almost entirely vowel sounds.

clue.text: Tiny bit in audiotape

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the word audiotape, spanning its middle letters

explanation.surface: A tiny fragment of sound recorded on a cassette.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, has come to mean a very small amount.

clue.text: Ordered Democratic president outside

indicators.note: the president's name goes around the letter for Democratic

parts.note: Joe Biden, US president

explanation.surface: A Democrat president gives orders from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidden is the past participle of bid, meaning commanded or told to do something.

clue.text: Once a TV broadcast is ready, used in some countries

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Once a television programme goes out, someone is prepared for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective, but in British slang 'the ready' is cash, and a centavo is a coin used in several Latin American countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The centavo is a small coin, a hundredth of a peso or similar currency, so it is money in those countries.

clue.text: Like solo organ performance in audition

definitions.text: Like solo organ performance in audition

parts.words: Like solo organ performance in audition
parts.note: the organ is the ear; hearing with one ear alone is a solo performance by that organ

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a musician playing the organ at an audition, but the organ is the ear and audition is hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaural means using or relating to a single ear, or a single sound channel.

clue.text: Comedians disturbed about upper-class lying

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go around the upper-class letter
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of comedians are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stand-up comics, upset, telling falsehoods about the posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacious means untruthful or given to telling falsehoods.

clue.text: In heartless prison, I lowered blind

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering a letter moves it further down the word
the central letter of the nine-letter prison word is removed

parts.note: a jailhouse is a prison
the letter I named in the clue

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a cruel jail drops a window shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the H out of the middle of JAILHOUSE, giving JAILOUSE; 'I lowered' then moves the I further down, to just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalousie is a window blind or shutter with angled slats.

clue.text: Food processor that is broken by small people

parts.note: the colon is part of the gut, which processes food

indicators.note: broken by means split open, with the small letter inside

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A kitchen food processor that small people have broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' looks like a kitchen gadget; it is the colon, part of the digestive tract. 'People' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a land is to fill it with inhabitants, which is what colonising does.

clue.text: Final letters backed wise work plan

indicators.note: backed means read backwards, so the whole combination is reversed

parts.note: a sage is wise; also used adjectivally
MO, modus operandi, is a method of working

explanation.surface: Closing letters supported a sensible working method.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so omegas are endings.

clue.text: Poet joins volunteers providing cover for knight

indicators.note: joins means the poet word is attached after the volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet signs up with the reserves to protect a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic worn by knights over armour, bearing their arms.

clue.text: Start to grow capital, having got rid of a pest

indicators.note: got rid of means removed, so these letters drop out of the capital

parts.note: Budapest is the capital of Hungary

explanation.surface: A city starts flourishing once it is free of a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bud is to sprout or begin developing, as a plant puts out shoots.

clue.text: Sign of distress as fall follows sprint

indicators.note: follows puts the fall word after the sprint word

parts.note: to tear is to rush or race
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting then tumbles, showing they are upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop shows sadness or anguish in someone crying.

clue.text: Greek letter in religious painting, not the consonant

indicators.note: not means without, so the consonant letter is left out

parts.note: a pietà depicts Mary holding the dead Christ
pi is a Greek letter, and a consonant one

explanation.surface: A Greek character appears in an icon, minus a consonant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The consonant' is itself a Greek letter, PI, taken from the front of PIETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Possible need for invalid inferior writer switching contents

indicators.note: switching means swapping, so the middle letter of the inferior word trades places with the writer's

parts.note: bad means inferior

indicators.note: contents names what is swapped: each short word's middle, its inside letter

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A poor author swaps material around; an invalid may need help.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD PEN has middle letters A and E; 'switching contents' swaps them, giving BED and PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpan is used by a patient confined to bed, someone too ill to get up.

clue.text: Delivery info initially upset person

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: DOB is the initials of date of birth, information about one's delivery

explanation.surface: Initial details about a parcel delivery upset someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is birth, not a parcel: date of birth abbreviates to DOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is British informal for a person or body, as in 'an odd bod'.

clue.text: Pitch checker's routine nap disturbed

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a disturbed nap is broken up, so its letters with routine's are mixed

explanation.surface: A routine afternoon sleep is interrupted by someone checking a cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner adjusts strings so that each note sounds at the correct pitch.

clue.text: Unusually veracious, apart from one piece that's bad for circulation

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
one is U, as in you, the generic person; a single piece of the word is left out

explanation.surface: Someone oddly truthful except about one item that harms blood flow.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of VERACIOUS, set U aside, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Varicose veins are swollen and twisted, impairing the flow of blood.

clue.text: Deny having daughter's ring put in a car?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, and the 's stands for is

indicators.note: put in means the ring letter goes inside the car letters

parts.note: A plus VW, the Volkswagen car
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone denies their daughter's engagement ring was left in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow is to refuse to acknowledge or to repudiate something.

clue.text: Wear thin, possibly becoming bare

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Clothing worn threadbare, leaving someone exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an idiom meaning naked or unclothed.

clue.text: Holes launches

definitions.meaning: second sense: premieres or first nights, as when a show opens

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gaps in something and inaugural events at which things start.

clue.text: Deployed joint force European commanded, holding weapon

indicators.note: holding means the commanded word wraps around the weapon

parts.note: led means commanded
a bow is a weapon

explanation.surface: A European commander deployed a combined military force carrying arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint force' looks military; the joint is the elbow, used to shove.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push them with the arm's middle joint.

clue.text: What I must have, but not in that case

definitions.text: What I must have, but not in that case

parts.words: What I must have, but not in that case
parts.note: a lowercase i carries a mark above it, but the capital or upper case letter does not

explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is the printing sense: lower case i has the mark, upper case I does not.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is the small point written above a lowercase i or j.

clue.text: Sections of vessels with three parts removed

definitions.text: Sections of vessels with three parts removed

parts.words: Sections of vessels with three parts removed
parts.note: the full name of these ship sections, contracted by dropping three bits replaced by apostrophes

explanation.walkthrough: The full word is FORECASTLES; the sailor's contraction FO'C'SLES drops RE, A and T, the three parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fo'c'sle is the forward part of a ship where the crew traditionally lived.

clue.text: Willing to admit nothing after the atom disintegrated

indicators.note: after puts the nothing letter at the end
disintegrated means broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A scientist willingly confesses that zero remained once the atom split.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at home to visitors is to be ready to receive them, letting them in.

clue.text: Neither posted nor moved?

parts.note: a letter not mailed, and also someone not sent, that is, not thrilled or carried away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' is old slang for thrilled or moved emotionally, so the word works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsent describes mail not dispatched, and playfully someone not transported with delight.

clue.text: What's German city got that Irish quarter hasn't?

definitions.text: What's German city got that Irish quarter hasn't?

parts.words: What's German city got that Irish quarter hasn't?
parts.note: Münster in Germany has two dots over its u; Munster, one of Ireland's four provinces, has none

explanation.walkthrough: Ireland has four provinces, so Munster is a quarter; the German city Münster is spelt the same except for the mark over the u.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the two-dot mark over a German vowel showing a change in sound.

clue.text: Female contributing to the website we've viewed regularly

indicators.note: the letters contribute to the phrase, sitting across the first two words

explanation.surface: A woman posts on a site we visit often.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'the website'; the rest of the phrase is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is the female of the sheep, so the general word names it by its sex alone, a definition by broad category.

clue.text: Valley's width in metric unit

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in puts the width letter inside the unit abbreviation

parts.note: cm is the centimetre, a metric unit

explanation.surface: A valley's breadth measured in metric units.
explanation.definitionFit: A cwm is a Welsh word for a valley or a rounded mountain hollow, a cirque.

clue.text: Second question in 30 — answer's 'trees'

indicators.note: in puts the question letter inside the answer to 30

parts.note: the answer to clue 30, a Bacchic cry
A is the abbreviation for answer, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A quiz with a second question about trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequoias are giant coniferous trees of California, among the tallest in the world.

clue.text: A youth going on lake for sail

indicators.note: going on means following, so the A and the youth come after the lake letter

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A young person takes to the lake to go sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lateen is a triangular sail on a long yard, used on dhows and feluccas.

clue.text: Dance costume pronounced excessively dated

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase given

parts.note: too-too is an old-fashioned expression for excessively or affectedly so

explanation.surface: An outfit for ballet is said to be badly out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by ballerinas.

clue.text: Frenzied expression as English promise to pay up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an IOU is a written promise to repay a debt

explanation.surface: An Englishman's wild cry as he settles a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Euoi is the ecstatic cry of Bacchic revellers in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Nasty person curate had to endure? Not entirely

definitions.text: Nasty person curate had to endure? Not entirely

parts.words: Nasty person curate had to endure? Not entirely
parts.note: alludes to the curate's egg, good in parts, so not entirely bad

explanation.walkthrough: In a Punch cartoon a curate, served a stale egg, says that parts of it are excellent; a curate's egg is something only partly bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an untrustworthy or unpleasant person.

clue.text: What's old in phony antique? Solve that!

indicators.note: phony means fake, so the letters are rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: An antiques dealer is challenged to say what's old about a fake piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An equation is a mathematical statement that you are asked to solve for its unknowns.
